hook_text: Why is part of Africa green on the map and part of it brown?
clip_script: Bloemfontein, high on the plateau, with frost on the school field. Two maps of Africa. One shows countries. The other shows the land itself: a physical map. Its colours are a code for height. Green is low, near sea level. Yellow and orange are higher. Brown is highest. Sea level is zero metres, and Kilimanjaro rises five thousand eight hundred and ninety-five metres above it. Rivers are blue lines, always flowing downhill.
visual_style: Whiteboard map of Africa filling in with colour layers, a key building beside it, and blue rivers drawing themselves to the sea.
mood: Calm and clever, like cracking a colour code.
pacing: Slow colour fill from low to high, then quick blue lines for rivers.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the highest and lowest places on your own atlas map.
